Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 unique messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01. I filtered on sender, recipient and date range. The 6 results had 6 distinct IDs, so none were duplicates. Dana is a direct recipient on some and one of several recipients on others. I'm listing five of the six IDs as sources.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05, with 23. I counted the sender's messages in September 2001 by UTC date. There were 160 in all. The next busiest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16.

I only have one message ID to cite, E80e4adf85ec0. It is the first message in the result set, not specifically one from 09-05.

ANSWER: 2001-09-05
SOURCES: E80e4adf85ec0

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard B Sanders in that window. I filtered for messages with richard.sanders@enron.com in To or Cc from 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05. That returned 37 messages, and I counted them by sender. Dasovich sent 8. The next highest was Susan Mara with 5.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd, E89c6a95fd0e2, Eaa28b1519008

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages in April 2001 to vkaminski@aol.com, with 173 unique messages. I counted a message once if the address was in To or Cc. His own address, vince.kaminski@enron.com, came second at 135.

I pulled all 458 messages he sent that month from vince.kaminski@enron.com. I then counted unique messages per recipient address.

The next three were shirley.crenshaw@enron.com (54), vasant.shanbhogue@enron.com (36) and stinson.gibner@enron.com (32). I didn't open any messages to read them. The source IDs below are only the examples my script stored for these addresses.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES: Ea8262445477a, Ebb15893fb393, E666e7353d570, Ee46106e51b86

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages on 2001-04-25, with 47. I counted messages from vince.kaminski@enron.com in April 2001 by UTC date. The next highest days were 2001-04-11 with 37 and 2001-04-27 with 36. I didn't open any individual messages, so the source list is empty.

ANSWER: 2001-04-25
SOURCES:

The reference ORE-7509 appears in one message, **E2083b9620d07**. It was sent on 2002-02-27 with the subject "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP".

The sender is marketing@nymex.com, shown as "Exchange Information @ENRON". The message is in the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s. The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)", so the reference belongs to a person named in the notice. That person isn't the sender.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07

The only message that mentions 703-227-8777 is **Ef817f5aac97c**. The number appears in it as "703.227.8777 Phone".

- **Sender:** Bryant Frihart (bryant.frihart@enron.com)
- **Date:** 2001-08-24
- **Subject:** "FW: 082501 Enron Confirmation"
- **Recipients:** To hayhurstb@paceglobal.com. Cc tammy.gilmore@enron.com and c..giron@enron.com.

I searched for the number with a pattern that allows dashes, dots, spaces and parentheses between the digits. That search returned this one message.

ANSWER: bryant.frihart@enron.com
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c

The exact string "EB-2934", with the hyphen, appears in only one message. The other eight matches write the room as "EB2934", without a hyphen.

That message is E2093dccd9417, "PSEG Meeting", dated 2000-12-05. Robin Barbe sent it to Chris Germany and Dick Jenkins. It places a meeting about 50,000/d at Transco Zone 6 "on Tuesday, December 5, 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934." So the reference is a conference room in the Enron Building, not a case or ticket number.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417

In November 2001, 14 distinct sender addresses sent at least one message containing "Raptor". I ran a case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message from 2001-11-01 up to but not including 2001-12-01. It matched 29 messages, and I counted the distinct `from` addresses across all of them.

The 14 addresses are:
- jr..legal@enron.com
- j.kaminski@enron.com
- milagros.velasquez@enron.com
- tom.fischbach@enron.com
- sean.riordan@enron.com
- rakesh.bharati@enron.com
- james.derrick@enron.com
- no.address@enron.com
- m..schmidt@enron.com
- surfn.go@americawest.com
- christian.yoder@enron.com
- rick.buy@enron.com
- tim.belden@enron.com
- vkaminski@aol.com

I counted addresses exactly as they appear, so j.kaminski@enron.com and vkaminski@aol.com count separately even though they may be the same person. I didn't open any messages to check the context of the matches. I'm not citing any source messages, because the count comes from the grep totals rather than from individual messages.

ANSWER: 14
SOURCES:

In December 2000, the sender who sent the most messages containing "Azurix" was enron.announcements@enron.com, with 7. A case-insensitive search of the full text of every message, headers included, returned 35 unique messages in that window. I counted them by sender address. The next highest was jeffrey.shankman@enron.com with 5.

I didn't open any individual messages to read them. The ids below are the ones I'm confident support the answer, but I haven't checked them against the announcement messages specifically.

ANSWER: enron.announcements@enron.com
SOURCES:

On 2000-05-23, 14 messages in the corpus contain "Dynegy" (case-insensitive, headers included). That is the most of any day in May 2000. I found them with a case-insensitive text search over the whole month. It matched 103 messages in total, and I counted them by UTC date. The next-highest days were 2000-05-04 and 2000-05-19, with 10 each.

ANSWER: 2000-05-23
SOURCES:
